review_candidates.title: Asset Management Section Head
review_candidates.description: Job Purpose To lead and oversee the strategic implementation and continuous optimization of the asset management system (IBM Maximo), ensuring accurate asset data, effective maintenance strategies, and integration with key enterprise functions. The role is responsible for developing asset hierarchies, managing lifecycle strategies, supporting cross-functional collaboration, and ensuring compliance with international standards such as ISO 55000. Through data-driven decision-making, system enhancements, and stakeholder engagement, the Head of Asset Management ensures the reliability, performance, and cost-effectiveness of assets across the organization. Responsibilities/Duties Profil de candidat recherché : Asset Management Strategy & Leadership Lead the end-to-end implementation of IBM Maximo, including planning, system configuration, testing, data migration, user acceptance testing, and go-live support. Define and manage asset hierarchies, classifications, attributes, and lifecycle strategies within the Maximo system. Ensure alignment of asset management objectives with broader corporate goals by working collaboratively with engineering, IT, operations, and finance teams. Drive continuous improvement of asset management practices and tools to meet evolving business needs and user expectations. System Integration & Optimization Oversee the seamless integration of Maximo with enterprise systems such as procurement, finance, and SCADA, ensuring efficient data exchange and process alignment. Lead the design, development, and implementation of Maximo workflows, automated alerts, and escalation procedures to streamline asset-related processes. Conduct impact assessments for requested Maximo customizations and lead user acceptance testing to validate changes before deployment. Data Governance & Reporting Manage the collection, cleansing, validation, and ongoing maintenance of asset data to ensure accuracy, integrity, and completeness. Monitor and report on KPIs related to asset performance, availability, lifecycle costs, and maintenance history. Analyze trends in asset performance and maintenance data to support planning for preventive actions, capital replacement, and risk mitigation strategies. Maintenance Strategy Development Design and implement preventive, corrective, and condition-based maintenance strategies using Maximo’s PM module to enhance asset reliability and optimize lifecycle cost. Training, Support & Compliance Provide comprehensive training, documentation, and ongoing support to Maximo users, ensuring effective system adoption and usage. Act as the primary point of contact for troubleshooting and user support related to Maximo functionality and reporting. Ensure asset management processes and system usage comply with ISO 55000 standards and other applicable frameworks. Safety Responsibilities Promote a positive safety culture within the workplace and attend any safety-related meetings or briefings as required within the job role. Comply with the requirements of RDMC RQHSE Policy and Safety Management System. Be mindful that Safety, Security, and Environmental protection are everyone’s responsibility. All staff members are accountable for reporting and intervening in any Safety, Security, or Environmental violations. Qualifications ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field. Fluent in English and Arabic, French is a plus. Knowledge Familiarity with ISO 55000, reliability-centered maintenance (RCM), and lifecycle asset planning. Experience in data governance, asset hierarchy design, and CMMS best practices. Certification in Maximo or asset management (e.g., IAM Certificate, Maximo Certified Professional) is preferred. Experience From 7 to 10 years of experience in asset management, maintenance systems, or reliability engineering. Proven experience implementing and managing IBM Maximo in large-scale industrial or infrastructure environments. Desired Behaviors & Experiences Strategic Thinking: Demonstrates a long-term, data-driven approach to asset management, aligning system capabilities and practices with organizational goals. Analytical Mindset: Uses asset performance data to drive decisions, identify risks, and recommend improvements in maintenance and lifecycle strategies. Collaboration and Influence: Builds strong relationships with cross-functional teams (engineering, IT, operations, finance) to ensure alignment and support for asset management initiatives. Continuous Improvement Focus: Proactively identifies system enhancements and process improvements based on evolving business needs and user feedback. Accountability: Takes full ownership of asset data integrity, system performance, and compliance with applicable standards such as ISO 55000. Effective Communication: Clearly conveys technical information and recommendations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Leadership by Example: Leads the asset management team with professionalism and integrity, fostering a culture of performance, innovation, and responsibility. Customer-Centric Approach: Supports end-users through training, troubleshooting, and documentation, ensuring high system usability and satisfaction.

This strategic transformation is committed to sustainable growth by putting people and the planet at the heart of our operations. In North Africa, this includes initiatives in responsible sourcing, waste reduction, and water conservation. Our regional programs empower local talent, boost employment, and provide support for local agriculture, particularly through partnerships with farmers and suppliers. Empowering Our People and Communities Our dynamic teams drive the PepsiCo culture in North Africa, embracing diversity and collaboration to solve local challenges and create innovative products. We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace, one where every individual feels valued and empowered to be themselves. This commitment extends beyond our employees to positively impact the communities we serve, striving for shared growth and a healthier, more sustainable future for all. The Utilities Engineer is responsible for ensuring the continuous, efficient, and reliable operation of all plant utility systems, including boilers, air compressors, chillers, cooling towers, water treatment units, and wastewater systems. The role supports production by providing uninterrupted utilities, improving efficiency, reducing energy consumption, and ensuring full compliance with PepsiCo safety and quality standards. Responsibilities Operations & Monitoring Ensure daily operation, monitoring, and control of utilities systems (steam, air, HVAC, chilled water, refrigeration, WWTP,….etc). Track utilities KPIs such as energy consumption, water usage, steam efficiency, and specific power consumption. Monitor SCADA systems and respond to alarms and deviations. Preventive & Corrective Maintenance Develop and implement preventive maintenance plans for utilities equipment. Troubleshoot mechanical and electrical failures in utilities equipment. Coordinate with maintenance teams for timely execution of corrective actions. SAP PM & Maintenance Management Create, update, and close notifications and work orders through SAP PM. Ensure accurate logging of maintenance activities, spare parts consumption, and equipment history. Analyze SAP PM reports to track breakdown frequency, MTTR, MTBF, and plan PM compliance. Support maintenance planning by identifying required spare parts and raising purchase requisitions. Reliability & Continuous Improvement Identify opportunities to reduce energy and water consumption. Improve equipment reliability through root cause analysis (RCA) and proactive actions. Support new utilities projects, upgrades, and capacity expansions. Safety, Compliance & Documentation Ensure full compliance with PepsiCo GEHSMS, ISO,FM Global, and regulatory standards. Maintain all utilities documentation (SOPs, logs, calibration records, permits). Conduct risk assessments and support process safety management (PSM). Cross-functional Support Provide utilities support during production shutdowns/startups. Coordinate with Production, Quality, EHS, and Engineering Departments. Manage external vendors and contractors for utilities systems. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, Electrical, or Mechatronics Engineering. 1–3 years of experience in utilities systems (FMCG or food & beverage preferred). Strong knowledge of: Boilers & steam systems Air compressors Chillers & refrigeration systems HVAC & cooling towers Water treatment (RO, softening, filtration) Wastewater treatment
